title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 37
paragraphs: Having built the wall across the neck of the Chersonese and thus repelled the Apsinthians, Miltiades first of all made war on the people of Lampsacus; and the people of Lampsacus laid an ambush and took him prisoner. Now Miltiades had come to be a friend of Croesus the Lydian; and Croesus accordingly, being informed of this event, sent and ordered the people of Lampsacus to let Miltiades go—otherwise he threatened to destroy them utterly like a pine tree. When the people of Lampsacus were at a loss in their deliberations as to what this saying meant with which Croesus had threatened them—that he would destroy them utterly like a pine tree—at length one of the elder men with some difficulty grasped the truth, and said that the pine alone of all trees, when it has been cut down, puts forth no further growth but perishes, being utterly destroyed. The people of Lampsacus, then, fearing Croesus, released Miltiades and let him go.
